messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — PrivateConnect VPN sessions to eu-west-2b showing route withdraws and intermittent reachability for customers on dedicated VPCs. Severity: possible customer impact. Auto-paged oncall.

jordan_k (oncall): I'm on it. seeing alerts from BGP monitor too. markers: multiple withdraws for customer prefixes originated from our vpn-gw-euw2b.

anya_m (netops): I can confirm — BGP peering state flaps between 10:23 and 10:29 across two sessions. AS_PATH shows repeated 65534 prepends then immediate withdraws.

sam_r (eng-sre): Any Cloud provider notice? Could be maintenance or noisy router in the AZ.

cloud-noc: We have a correlated telemetry spike in eu-west-2b peering routers at ~10:22 UTC — hardware queueing. Opening a ticket with backbone team. Reference INC-8721.

jordan_k (oncall): Assigning SEV-2 for customer impact on PrivateConnect/VPN. Lina, can you start drafting customer comms for affected accounts? target initial ack in 15m.

lina_cs (customer-success): On it. Which customers are impacted? I have a short list from the routing alerts.

sam_r (eng-sre): Posting quick diagnostic: ```
# bgp-summary vpn-gw-euw2b
Neighbor 192.0.2.18    AS 65010  State: Established
Prefixes  48            Advertised
LastErr  0
--
# bgp-routes | grep 198.51.100.0/24
198.51.100.0/24  withdrawn at 2026-03-12T10:24:06Z
198.51.100.0/24  announced at 2026-03-12T10:25:12Z via 65010
``` 

anya_m (netops): Looks like paths are being suppressed by an upstream policy — likely because of route dampening triggered by repeated withdraws. I can temp-disable dampening for the affected neigh if we approve.

jordan_k (oncall): Do it. Disable dampening for the two affected neighbors and watch for stabilization. Also enable the backup tunnel for customers on the secondary egress (eu-west-1 fallback) where configured.

anya_m (netops): Done: disabled dampening on routes to 192.0.2.18 and 192.0.2.19. Triggered backup -> issuing route re-advertise. ETA ~ 90s.

deploy-bot: vpn-config-job-442 applied to vpn-gw-euw2b: backup-tunnel-policy enabled by oncall (jordan_k).

sam_r (eng-sre): I'm seeing prefixes re-announce. Packet-loss metrics for affected customers dropped from 12%->1.2% after correction. Still seeing occasional spikes.

lina_cs (customer-success): Sending initial notification to impacted accounts: "We're investigating degraded connectivity to eu-west-2b PrivateConnect endpoints. Workaround applied — we have enabled backup tunnels and are working with provider to restore stable routing. We'll update in 30 minutes." Will post in ticket.

cloud-noc: We pushed a control-plane fix at 10:31 UTC for the backlog on the routing engine. They believe the root cause: transient queue exhaustion on a line-card causing BGP to flap; they replaced the card in a rolling fashion.

jordan_k (oncall): Good. Can we mark mitigation in place? I want to hand off to night oncall in 40m. We need a clear action list: 1) monitor routes for 2h, 2) keep dampening disabled until flare subsides, 3) follow up with provider RCA.

anya_m (netops): Adding to runbook: run `bgp-watch --peer 192.0.2.18 --threshold 3m` and alert if >3 withdraws in 5m. Also capture tcpdumps for a sample customer session for postmortem.

sam_r (eng-sre): Captured pcap snippet — uploading to incident artifact store: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/incidents/1769123456/pcap.tar.gz

lina_cs (customer-success): Customer A acknowledged workaround and will keep team updated if they see issues. Customer B reported brief timeouts but confirmed failover worked.

jordan_k (oncall): Preparing handoff note for @night_oncall: "Mitigation: dampening disabled on affected peers; backup tunnels enabled; provider replaced line-card. Monitor BGP announcements/withdraws for affected prefixes; keep customer comms open. Severity lowered to SEV-3 pending 2h stability."

night_oncall (placeholder): I see handoff. I'll pick this up at 23:00 UTC.

cloud-noc: Provider will deliver formal RCA within 24h. They flagged that bursty prefixes from a third-party peer amplified dampening effects. Working with them to tune thresholds.

anya_m (netops): Note: we should consider removing our aggressive prefix-limited dampening in favour of per-customer exceptions. I'll open a config change request with infra.

sam_r (eng-sre): For postmortem, capture: timeline of withdraws, dampening triggers, provider HW replacement time, customer impact windows, and why backup tunnels didn't fully remove all timeouts for some sessions.

lina_cs (customer-success): I'll coordinate customer follow-ups once RCA is in. Drafting post-incident email for customers impacted by route instability.

jordan_k (oncall): Closing loop: current status = degraded -> mitigated. Will keep thread updated. If we see >2 withdraw events in 10m, re-escalate to SEV-2 and re-page network leads.

incident-bot: SEV state changed to SEV-3 at 10:33 UTC by jordan_k (oncall). Next update scheduled at 11:00 UTC or on new event.

sam_r (eng-sre): Leaving final note before handoff: metrics spike correlated with queue drops at provider, our mitigation reduced blackholing, but we need provider RCA and a config change to avoid future false-positive dampening. Marking for postmortem.

jordan_k (oncall): Handoff completed to night_oncall. Thanks all — clean handoff and follow-ups in the notes. :thumbsup:

lina_cs (customer-success): Posting customer update 10:40 UTC: "Issue mitigated; provider is performing hardware work; we will share RCA within 24 hours. Contact support for any regressions." 

cloud-noc: Follow-up: INC-8721 updated with provider ticket ID PROV-4492.

incident-bot: Thread archived by jordan_k (oncall) at 10:43 UTC.
